clue.text: Masculine violence without one display of animosity

parts.note: masculine means male

indicators.note: without tells us to drop a letter from the word violence

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A man's violence is described as a show of hostility.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Masculine violence' reads as one idea, but 'without one' strips the Roman I from the second word before it follows the first.
explanation.definitionFit: Malevolence is ill will shown towards others, a display of hostility.

clue.text: Shrewd but pointless search

indicators.note: pointless says a compass point, here south-east, is removed from the word search

explanation.surface: A fruitless hunt is called cunning.
explanation.walkthrough: SE (south-east) is a point of the compass, so 'pointless' search loses it, leaving the remainder.
explanation.definitionFit: Arch as an adjective means knowing or cunning, like a sly, mischievous look.

clue.text: My desire must be to see mine scattered

definitions.text: My desire must be to see mine scattered

indicators.note: scattered means the letters of see mine are thrown about into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone states their wish to watch their foes routed.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both definition and wordplay: the foes one wishes to see routed are 'mine', and SEE MINE rearranged gives them.
explanation.definitionFit: The people a person most wants to see routed are their foes or adversaries.

clue.text: Does Paddy's new appeal upset him?

indicators.note: upset in a down clue turns the word new upside down, so it reads backwards

parts.note: taken as written
O is an exclamation of appeal, as in 'O Lord'

explanation.surface: A political question: will Paddy Ashdown's fresh appeal annoy his rival?
explanation.walkthrough: Written when Paddy Ashdown led the Liberal Democrats and David Owen the rival SDP; 'him' points to that politician. 'upset' reverses NEW plus O as one run.
explanation.definitionFit: The pronoun points to David, the SDP leader who was Paddy Ashdown's rival in British politics.

clue.text: Save up before I have to become off-putting

indicators.note: up in a down clue tells us to read the word save from the bottom upwards

parts.note: taken as written
've is the short form of have

explanation.surface: Someone saves money first before turning unhelpful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Save' reads as a verb about money, but it is fodder; 'up' turns it over in this down clue, and 'before' sets it ahead of the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Evasive answers put a questioner off, dodging and deflecting.

clue.text: Dog food

definitions.meaning: a breed of dog from China with a blue-black tongue
slang for grub or eats

explanation.definitionFit: A Chinese breed of dog shares its name with slang for something to eat.

clue.text: Important instruction to one's financial attorney

definitions.meaning: meaning notable or weighty
read as a phrase: what you tell someone holding power of attorney to do on your behalf, put your name to it should you be unable

explanation.walkthrough: Split as SIGN IF I CAN'T, it is what you would tell someone holding power of attorney.
explanation.definitionFit: Significant means of consequence; split up it is a request to sign when you are not able.

clue.text: Sole motor car component used in nuclear research

definitions.meaning: the car pedal pressed by the sole of the foot to go faster
a machine that speeds up particles for physics experiments

explanation.definitionFit: The throttle pedal under the driver's foot and a particle-speeding machine in physics labs share the name.

clue.text: He plays with unnoted companies in part of an opera

indicators.note: in places the shortened companies inside the part of an opera

parts.note: an opera is divided into acts

indicators.note: unnoted says a musical note, here E, is taken out of the word companies

explanation.surface: A musician performs alongside unsung troupes in a stretch of an opera.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unnoted' drops the musical note E; 'in' places what remains inside the act. 'He plays with' describes a pianist backing a soloist.
explanation.definitionFit: A pianist who backs a singer or soloist plays along with them.

clue.text: Pick me up with the others to deliver a speech about four

parts.note: the rest means the others

indicators.note: about means going around, so the speech-making word encloses the four

parts.note: to orate is to make a speech
IV is four in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Someone offers a tonic, joining the group to make a speech about the number four.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pick me up' looks like an instruction but is the definition, a tonic; 'about' sets the speech word around the Roman four.
explanation.definitionFit: A tonic or drink that revives you, a pick-me-up, is a restorative.

clue.text: Disorderly venues offer up a husbandman's prayer

definitions.meaning: rowdy, chaotic places, originally where bears were baited
split as two words, a farmer or gardener praying that his plots will yield crops

explanation.walkthrough: A husbandman is a farmer; read as BEAR, GARDENS! it is his plea for crops. 'offer up' just links.
explanation.definitionFit: Rowdy scenes are bear gardens; split up, the words are a grower's plea that his plots yield.

clue.text: Extremely small island

definitions.meaning: a tiny amount or distance
a Scottish word for a small island

explanation.walkthrough: In Scotland an INCH is a small island, as in Inchcolm in the Firth of Forth.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiny measure of length shares its name with the Scots term for an islet.

clue.text: In short, we are what we used to be

definitions.meaning: the contraction of two words into one with an apostrophe
the past tense of are, used with we

explanation.definitionFit: Without its apostrophe the contraction of 'we are' is the past form of the verb to be.

clue.text: Is it their stupidity which lands them in the soup?

definitions.text: Is it their stupidity which lands them in the soup?

parts.words: Is it their stupidity which lands them in the soup?
parts.note: fools land in trouble through folly, while strips of pasta land literally in soup; the word means both simpletons and pasta

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both simpletons and the pasta strips that go into soup.

clue.text: Weapon made from spare parts

indicators.note: parts suggests the word spare is broken into pieces and reassembled

explanation.surface: An arm is assembled out of leftover components.
explanation.definitionFit: A long pole with a pointed head, thrown or thrust in battle, is a weapon.

clue.text: He flies from America by way of hill

parts.note: via means by way of
a tor is a rocky hill, especially on Dartmoor

explanation.surface: Someone travels by air from the States, routed over a hill.
explanation.definitionFit: A pilot is someone who flies an aircraft.

clue.text: Excuse offered by criminal is a liberal one

parts.note: I is one in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A crook's story claims he is a free-thinking sort.
explanation.definitionFit: A suspect's claim to have been elsewhere at the time of a crime is his excuse.

clue.text: Tap a Pole having a nap

parts.note: S stands for the South Pole
pile is the raised nap of a fabric or carpet

explanation.surface: A Polish man is roused from a doze.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pole' tempts as a nationality, but it is a compass pole, S.
explanation.definitionFit: A spile is a wooden peg or spigot used as a tap in a cask.

clue.text: Chemist stocks nothing for dandies

indicators.note: stocks means holds within, so the chemist's letters contain the nothing

parts.note: FPS: Fellow of the Pharmaceutical Society
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A pharmacist has empty shelves for the well-dressed men.
explanation.walkthrough: FPS (Fellow of the Pharmaceutical Society) is an old abbreviation for a chemist.
explanation.definitionFit: Fops are vain men excessively concerned with clothes, like dandies.

clue.text: Song which upsets a terrorist organisation

indicators.note: upsets turns the whole of a plus the terrorist group backwards

parts.note: the IRA, the Irish Republican Army

explanation.surface: A tune that offends a militant group.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upsets' reverses A IRA as one run.
explanation.definitionFit: An aria is a solo song in an opera.

clue.text: One with something to fear from Arab bigotry

indicators.note: from shows the letters are taken out of the run Arab bigotry

explanation.surface: A Jewish leader faces anti-Jewish prejudice from Arabs.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer sits across the two words aRAB BIgotry.
explanation.definitionFit: A Jewish religious teacher might fear hostility from Arab bigotry.

clue.text: Is sorry for king herons

parts.note: R is short for rex, king
egrets are a kind of heron

explanation.surface: A monarch's birds cause him to apologise.
explanation.definitionFit: Regrets means feels sorry about something.

clue.text: Ageing beauty's confession that she has reached a dead end

definitions.meaning: split as ..., a fading beauty admitting she is past her best
a deadlock or blind alley

explanation.definitionFit: An admission of being out of date, split in two, is also a deadlock or blind alley.

clue.text: It develops from fir cone

indicators.note: develops says the letters of fir cone grow into a new form

explanation.surface: A tree grows from a seed-bearing cone.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both definition and wordplay: a fir tree grows from its cone.
explanation.definitionFit: A fir is a cone-bearing evergreen tree, grown from the seed in its cone.

clue.text: Accused of having put in a crooked dime

indicators.note: in places the word put inside the mixed-up coin
crooked means bent or twisted, so the letters of dime are disordered

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone is charged with slipping in a bent coin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crooked' rearranges the coin to IMED; 'in' puts PUT inside. Imputed means attributed, as a charge laid at someone's door.
explanation.definitionFit: A fault imputed to someone is one laid at their door, a charge.

clue.text: Food in cafe with piped music blaring out?

definitions.meaning: slang for grub

definitions.text: in cafe with piped music blaring out?
definitions.meaning: split as ..., where loud music plays there is no hush

explanation.definitionFit: Slang for grub, split in two it says there is no hush in a noisy café.

clue.text: Stew pot

definitions.meaning: a dish of chopped cooked meat
slang for cannabis, also called hashish

explanation.definitionFit: A dish of chopped meat shares its name with slang for cannabis resin.

clue.text: Still one has not been captured in Tibet!

definitions.text: has not been captured in Tibet!

parts.note: yet means still
I is one in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: An exclamation that the creature still evades capture in the Himalayas.
explanation.definitionFit: The Abominable Snowman of the Himalayas has never been caught.

clue.text: New star arising as the flower of Stratford

indicators.note: arising means going up, so the new star word is read backwards

parts.note: a nova is a star that suddenly brightens

explanation.surface: A fresh star rises as the bloom of Shakespeare's town.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'flower' is something that flows, a river; Stratford-upon-Avon is Shakespeare's town.
explanation.definitionFit: The river running through Stratford is a flow-er, something that flows.

clue.text: sq metres to a certain extent

definitions.meaning: square metres measure a surface
a region or expanse

explanation.definitionFit: Square metres measure a surface's size, and the word also means a region of some extent.

clue.text: Flexible rule for pureeing a steam puree

indicators.note: pureeing means mashing up, so the letters of a steam puree are blended

explanation.surface: A cook wants a guideline for liquidising steamed food.
explanation.definitionFit: A bendable strip marked in inches or centimetres is a flexible ruler.

clue.text: If let out of the bag, it would doubtless raise a smile

definitions.text: If let out of the bag, it would doubtless raise a smile

parts.words: If let out of the bag, it would doubtless raise a smile
parts.note: the idiom of letting a cat out of the bag, combined with the grinning feline in Alice in Wonderland

explanation.definitionFit: The grinning feline in Lewis Carroll's Alice is famous for its smile.
